published_source: Figure 4, panel (d) of the published article (Management Science 71(11), 2025, pp. 9628-9649; papers/mnsc/mnsc.2020.01838.pdf): point estimates are plotted, not printed. authors_code_* = output of Replicate.R line 256 on the shipped data, which the figure plots. Panel labels checked against the article (Nov 2).
replication_status: exact (fixest with event_structure reproduces the authors' Replicate.R event coefficients on the authors' sample; pipeline sample drops the post-breakup bins, see event_structure.verified)
notes: Kang (2025), 'Price-Fixing Cartels and Firm Innovation', Management Science 71(11). Package: Replicate.R + final cleaned/merged .rds files (real processed data; raw DOJ/VitalLaw, PatentsView and licensed Compustat not shipped). FE: unit + 4-digit-NAICS (patents) or Compustat industry group (R&D) x year (authors: felm(... | assignee_id + paste0(cl, year) | 0 | cl)); here xt_vars = naics4 (= cl) so the time FE is year + year x cl; SE clustered by cl. No controls, no weights. Outcomes are IHS-transformed counts/amounts, precomputed as ihs_* (log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)), as in Replicate.R). Figure 4(b)/(d) 3-year-bin path, data_reg_patent.rds (612 treated assignees; bins 1_PreA = formation-relative years -7..-5, 2_PreB = -4..-2 (reference), 3_OnA = +1..+2, 4_OnB = +3..+8, 5_PostA/6_PostB/7_PostC = breakup-relative +1..+3/+4..+6/+7..+9; relative years -1 and 0 are not in the file). Ruling 5b(d): the post-breakup bins are dropped (collusion switches off at breakup; Hull fn 6), leaving a formation event study on 404 treated units (after the episode split). Bins (Nov 2, event_structure): the authors' three-year groups on the pipeline sample. Because rows at formation-relative -1 and 0 do not exist, gvar g_form_m1 = formation year - 1 (no observed row changes treatment status; gives CSA an observed base period), so rel = formation-relative year + 1: PreA rel -6..-4, PreB (reference) rel -3..-1, OnA rel 2..3, OnB rel 4..9. Authors' bins with all seven bins: see authors_code_event_coefs; with post-breakup bins dropped (pipeline sample, authors' FE): see binned_droppost_coefs. Unit id uid = assignee_id except for the one assignee in three cartel episodes (226bee8a..., formations 1988/1995/1998 with overlapping windows, the source of all duplicated assignee-years), which is split into three assignee x episode units so that every unit has one adoption date and no duplicated unit-years; this is the only difference from the authors' regression sample and FE. Nov 2 audit: event_structure records the authors' bins and reference; sample_filter 'pre_sample_adopter == FALSE' removed, pre-sample adopters kept at their true dates (gvar already holds the calendar year; no adoption_var needed). See the log's Nov 2 section.

event_structure.source: Replicate.R line 256: felm(depvar ~ TreatY + TreatY:factor(TimeGroup, levels = c('2_PreB','1_PreA','3_OnA','4_OnB','5_PostA','6_PostB','7_PostC')) | assignee_id + paste0(cl, year) | 0 | cl) on data_reg_patent.rds; 2_PreB is the first level and is dropped (collinear with the unit FE), so it is the reference (article, Figure 4 notes: Precollusion2 'serves as the baseline'). In the shipped file the groups are formation-relative years rf = year - ID_From (pre-breakup rows): PreA -7..-5, PreB -4..-2, OnA 1..2, OnB 3..8 (rf -1 and 0 absent; the article's text describes Precollusion2 as 1-3 years before and Collusion1 as 1-3 years after formation, the shipped TimeGroup is used). PostA/B/C are breakup-relative years 1-3/4-6/7-9, i.e. treatment switched off: their 2,472 treated rows are dropped (PROTOCOL 5b switch-off rule, Hull fn. 6; Nov 1 log ruling (d)). gvar g_form_m1 = ID_From - 1, so rel = t - g = rf + 1 in the annual period index (years 1976-2020 consecutive): PreA [-6,-4], ref PreB [-3,-1], OnA [2,3], OnB [4,9] (max observed rf 8). 'drop': the shipped file contains treated rows only inside the authors' coded window (the event year itself is omitted), so no ever-treated row falls outside bins and ref (0 rows, checked Nov 2); 'drop' and 'ref' are equivalent here. Pre-sample adopters (11 units with event year before 1976) are kept at their true date (gvar holds the calendar year; PROTOCOL Nov 2 ruling (b)); all their in-sample rows are post rows inside the window.
event_structure.verified: Published regression: fixest with the authors' seven TimeGroup indicators (reference 2_PreB; FE assignee_id + cl^year; cluster cl) on the full shipped data_reg_patent.rds (436,000 rows, incl. the pre-sample units) reproduces Replicate.R line 256 (PreA -0.0603, OnA 0.0667, OnB 0.1936, as plotted; max abs diff 4.9e-13); the post-breakup groups cannot be written as intervals of formation-relative time, so this check uses TimeGroup directly. The pipeline sample differs from the authors': the 2,472 post-breakup treated rows are dropped, which moves OnA/OnB to 0.0651/0.1215; on that sample fixest with this structure reproduces binned_droppost_coefs (max abs diff 1.2e-12; SE max diff 2.0e-05, felm vs fixest small-sample factor). Pipeline unit id (episode split of one multi-cartel assignee) moves the bins by at most 2.0e-03. No numbers are printed in the article; the figure plots the code output on the shipped data.

pipeline_sample_twfe_source: Nov 2: fixest on the pipeline sample (pre-sample adopters kept at true dates, uid FE + cl^year) with event_structure; post (pre) = equal-weight mean of the post_summary (pre_summary) bins, std = post / population SD of y over all estimation rows.
